          Not Yet an All-Rounder, But Match-Winner Alexander Isak Proving His Worth at Liverpool
        
      
                          
                      Oct 20, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
It was a third consecutive Premier League away game in which Alexander Isak scored the winner for Liverpool. The Swede is finally proving his worth after a turbulent first season on Merseyside.
All three of Liverpool’s wins in the Premier League this season have come on the road, and all three have been courtesy of winning goals from Alexander Isak.

Saturday always looked like it could be tough for Andoni Iraola’s men. Facing unbeaten Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium just three days after a European away game had all the hallmarks of a difficult afternoon.

The Bees beat Chelsea 3-0 in their previous home game, and Liverpool were coming into the contest off the back of a loss by the same score against Manchester City the previous weekend at Anfield. They scored six against LASK in the Champions League in midweek, but Keith Andrews’ side would surely present more of a challenge.

The first half didn’t exactly dampen those fears either. After Bradley Barcola missed a glorious one-on-one chance to give Liverpool the lead, they lost Dominik Szoboszlai to injury and had a penalty award overturned after a VAR review. Just moments later, Keane Lewis-Potter headed Brentford in front.

Everything was going wrong, until Yehor Yarmoliuk had a moment of madness and decided to headbutt Jérémy Jacquet while jostling ahead of a corner being taken. Unsurprisingly, he was shown a red card just before half-time.

That changed the game entirely, and in the second half, Liverpool took advantage. First, Florian Wirtz fed Víctor Muñoz, who raced away down the right, before chopping inside and finishing well to equalise.
Then eight minutes later, Isak, who had been quiet up to that point, controlled Barcola’s header back to him and finished well to score what ultimately proved to be the winner.
It wasn’t the first time Liverpool’s £125 million striker had not done much until he made the most important contribution of the game.

Isak’s first goal of the season was to equalise against Nottingham Forest on Matchday 2 at Anfield, while he hit a quickfire brace early on at Ipswich Town in what proved to be the only two goals of that victory.

He scored the only goal of the win at Bournemouth just before the international break, and though he missed the home defeat to Man City through injury picked up during that break, he was back in the starting line-up at Brentford, justifying his involvement with another winner.

There was, of course, a lot of attention after Isak’s move to Liverpool in the summer of 2025: the manner of how he left Newcastle United, the money involved, and a thoroughly underwhelming return in his first campaign on Merseyside.
A lack of pre-season, generally poor performances from Liverpool under Arne Slot, and terrible luck with injuries meant Isak produced just four goals in 22 games last season.
We’re only in mid-October and he already has five goals this season in just eight games.

He has already racked up a personal expected goals total (xG) of 4.1 in those eight games, just shy of the 4.2 he managed in 22 outings last season, while his xG per shot has gone up to 0.21 from 0.15, meaning he is taking his shots from much better positions on average.
More important than these numbers, though, is his ability to decide tight matches, and especially tricky away matches.

As Opta’s Michael Reid pointed out on X after the game, Isak became just the second Liverpool player in the 21st century to score the winning goal in three consecutive Premier League away games, after Roberto Firmino (Dec 2019 to Jan 2020).
Alexander Isak is only the second player in the 21st century to score the winner in 3 consecutive Premier League away games for Liverpool, after Roberto Firmino from Dec 2019 to Jan 2020. #LFC

Isak also continued his perfect record against Brentford. The Swede has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against the Bees (5 goals, 4 for Newcastle); only Erling Haaland vs Crystal Palace (6) has a better 100% rate in the competition.

That ability to be quiet in a game before pouncing to score a crucial goal is something Haaland gets praised for all the time, and rightly so. Isak perhaps had a reputation from his time at Newcastle for being more involved in build-up play, arguably more of an all-round forward than the Norwegian.
